purpose: Role map for compatibility benchmark files. This registry prevents development, calibration, and blind-reporting data from being mixed accidentally.
current_blind_status: Q12 was frozen on 2026-07-20 and is the current blind benchmark; it is UNSCORED. Its labels were sealed and SHA256-hashed before any prediction was run. Q11 produced the project's only genuine blind compatibility number (63.9% on 2026-07-20) and was then DEMOTED to spent_diagnostic because its errors directed scorer remediation the same day; its post-fix 69.7% is regression evidence only. Q8 and Q9 remain spent diagnostics. Q10 remains the sealed, unscored final exam and has never been consumed. Do not score Q12 until there is a reason to spend it.
rules: development datasets may be used for scorer changes and calibration
spent_diagnostic datasets may be used for error analysis, development, and calibration, but not as fresh blind claims
current_blind datasets may be run for reporting only and must not be used for scorer tuning or calibration
if a current_blind dataset is used for tuning or calibration, change its role to spent_diagnostic and freeze a new blind dataset

datasets.demotion_reason: Its first-run errors were used to direct scorer remediation (solvent intent, collector vetoes, cross-domain routing). Per registry rule, a current_blind dataset used for tuning becomes spent_diagnostic. The 2026-07-20 first_blind_run below remains the only genuine blind number Q11 will ever produce; the post_fix_regression_run is regression evidence, NEVER a blind claim.

post_fix_regression_run.honest_reading: Correct answers did NOT increase: 23 of 40 both before and after. Four genuine fixes were gained (S8+Cu_foil FP->TN via the collector veto; PEEK+Water FN->TP via curated uptake data; CMC+Water and Bi2Te3+Ni SKIP->TP via role threading and cross-domain routing) and four previously-correct answers became honest abstentions (PS/PC+Acetone, PDMS/PMMA+Toluene were right only because a constant 0.45 matched an incompatible label by base rate). Errors fell 13->10 and MCC rose 0.278->0.401, so the answers that ARE given are better; coverage fell 36->33 evaluated because the bridge now declines organic-solvent resistance instead of guessing. Accuracy-on-evaluated rising 63.9%->69.7% is partly a shrinking denominator and must not be quoted alone.

first_blind_run.note: First genuine current-blind compatibility result. Development 41/41 and Q9 87.5% do not predict blind performance. Errors concentrate in three mechanisms diagnosed on INDEPENDENT probe pairs: (1) solvent-exposure role missing from COEXISTENCE_INTERFACE_ROLES so the blend immiscibility veto fires inverted on chemical-resistance interfaces; (2) current-collector identity ignored in battery scoring; (3) cross-domain routing skips. Q11 is NOT yet spent - seeing results does not spend it, remediating against them does.

datasets.notes: Q11 frozen 2026-07-20. Zero material-name-pair overlap against blind_test_pairs, ground_truth, all prior external_blind (Q2-Q10), and all dev_compatibility files (checked programmatically against 485 existing name-pairs). All material names resolve in a bridge vocabulary, so skips cannot be caused by out-of-vocabulary names. LIMITATION: pairs reuse known materials in unused COMBINATIONS - this tests generalization to new pairings, not to new materials. LIMITATION: labels are expert judgment authored by the same AI assistant that worked on this codebase, sealed and hashed before prediction; this is weaker independence than an external labeler and is disclosed deliberately.

Q12 frozen 2026-07-20, immediately after Q11 was spent. NOT YET SCORED. Built around 12 CONTRAST GROUPS: two pairs sharing one material whose correct answers are opposite (e.g. PVDF+Acetone soluble vs PP+NMP insoluble; Ni+Mo weldable vs Al+Ti intermetallic). Q11 demonstrated that a constant fallback score passes a set dominated by 'incompatible' labels purely by base rate; a contrast group cannot be passed that way, because any constant scores both members identically and must get one wrong. Zero material-name-pair overlap against all 525 prior benchmark pairs (blind_test_pairs, ground_truth, Q2-Q11, dev_compatibility), verified programmatically at freeze. All names resolve in a bridge vocabulary. 11 pairs are flagged borderline in the sealed label file and should be reported separately from clear-cut ones. Same disclosed limitations as Q11: expert-judgment labels authored by the same assistant that worked on the codebase, sealed and hashed before prediction; known materials in unused combinations.
